transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

...They said I had to come in. Just... people say my talking gets all mixed up. I try to explain things to them. You know, about the keys... and then the jail... the prayer rug... chess pieces. I don't know. They just tell me they can't follow what I'm saying. So that's why I'm here.
About how long has this been happening, where people notice your speech getting mixed up?

I don't know exactly... maybe two years and five months. Give or take. It was after... well, there was a misunderstanding at the building. They detained me for a bit over it. Since around then, I guess.
Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually energetic or 'high,' needing much less sleep than usual?

Sometimes, I guess. I don't know about the word 'high.' Just... there are times I feel really good. Powerful, maybe. I'll laugh more, talk loud with folks. 

But... if someone starts questioning me about things, I... I can snap. Just shout at them over some small thing. That's... yeah, that happens sometimes.
Does the trouble with your speech happen even during times when your mood feels completely normal?

Yeah... I guess. There are weeks when things are just... calmer. I'm not feeling too big, and I'm not feeling low either. 

But... even then... like for a couple weeks or more... I still hear him. The man in the air vents. And I know the people in the building are still... signaling each other about me. So... yeah. It doesn't just stop.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out F31 because psychotic symptoms (hallucinations and delusions) persist for at least two weeks in the absence of prominent mood episodes, which meets criteria for schizoaffective disorder rather than bipolar disorder with psychotic features. Ruled out F20 due to prominent concurrent manic episodes.
